— Defensive Driving and Communication","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Defensive Driving and Communication

FACT_ID: sec14-F01 | anchor: A01
Defensive driving keeps you aware and ready, since 94 percent of serious crashes trace to human choices and errors [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec14-F02 | anchor: A01
First, think safety: shun aggression and inattention, bank space ahead, and belt against ejection [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec14-F03 | anchor: A01
Second, stay aware: sweep mirrors often, read 20 to 30 seconds ahead, and keep eyes roaming [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec14-F04 | anchor: A01
Dodge aggressive drivers by slowing, pulling over, or exiting safely, while tracking walkers, riders, and animals [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec14-F05 | anchor: A01
Third, trust no one: expect red-light and stop-sign runners and plan every move for the worst case [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec14-F06 | anchor: A01
Fourth, hold the 3- to 4-second gap for reaction room [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec14-F07 | anchor: A01
Fifth, temper speed to conditions below ideal-road limits, since pace erodes control when trouble strikes [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec14-F08 | anchor: A01
Sixth, bank an escape route: sit seen and seeing with an alternate path for sudden blocks [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec14-F09 | anchor: A01
Seventh, kill distractions and grant driving your whole mind [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec14-F10 | anchor: A02
Match traffic pace, since speed outliers breed lane swaps, passes, tailgating, and crashes; uniform lawful speed is safest [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec14-F11 | anchor: A02
Adapt pace early to slow traffic with lane moves or gentle braking, never sudden stomps [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec14-F12 | anchor: A02
Farm rigs, horse carts, ATVs, UTVs, and road crews creep, often flying orange triangles or flashers [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec14-F13 | anchor: A02
Tailgating kills stopping room, so judge gaps by the three-four-second rule with longer spans at speed [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec14-F14 | anchor: A02
When tailgated, edge right for their view, telegraph moves early, slow to invite a pass, or leave the flow [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec14-F15 | anchor: A03
Broadcast presence and plans, since unseen and surprising moves cause crashes [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec14-F16 | anchor: A03
Headlights show you the dark and show you to others, so burn them through fog, rain, and snow, overriding auto lamps in bright snow glare [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec14-F17 | anchor: A03
Iowa law lights both beams sunset to sunrise and whenever sight drops to 500 feet or less; wipers on means lights on [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec14-F18 | anchor: A03
Sound the horn for lane-drifting walkers and riders, passers swerving at you, inattentive or half-blind drivers, and blind alley mouths [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec14-F19 | anchor: A03
Also horn cars threatening you, anyone needing your presence announced, and your own runaway slides toward people [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec14-F20 | anchor: A03
Broken down, flee the roadway if able, blaze hazards, and park only where approaching eyes can see, never past crests or bends [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec14-F21 | anchor: A03
Stalled in a lane, march everyone out fast to ground far from shoulders and traffic, then call the authorities [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0049]

Misconceptions: matching traffic excuses speeding, yet limits still cap the flow; headlights serve only night sight, yet they also announce you by day; hazards alone save a stalled car, yet placement and exit matter more.

Mnemonic: safety first, eyes roaming, trust none, gap three, speed low, out ready, focus full; wipers on, lights on.

Glossary: escape route (an alternate path when yours blocks); tailgating (following too closely); hazard lights (flashers marking a troubled car); slow-moving vehicle sign (an orange triangle on creeping rigs).

Dynamic facts: none in these pages; every defensive and communication rule above is stable handbook knowledge with no date-variable or place-variable values.
